messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: Dedicated pool node dpool-us-e1-07 in pool=dedicated-lumenabio reported repeated GPU preemptions and nvlink errors — ongoing. severity=SEV2. paging maya (oncall).

maya (oncall): got it. seeing GPU ECC spikes + rapid container evictions. @jordan can you confirm hardware/unexpected preempt pattern?

jordan: looking. telemetry shows kernel oops on GPU1 then instant preempt by host. suspect spot/host reclaim? host metadata shows cloud provider preempt signal 2023-11-06T15:12Z. tenants: lumenabio-prod, lumenabio-staging.

eli (noc): customer impact? are requests failing or degraded?

elena (CS - LumenaBio): we're getting alerts — customers reporting higher tail latency on embeddings endpoints. some jobs retried and queued. major pipeline backfills paused. please advise mitigation asap.

maya (oncall): immediate mitigation: isolate node, start live drain for tenant pods and failover traffic to fallback pool. steps:
```
# mark node unschedulable
kubectl cordon dpool-us-e1-07
# move tenant pods (force eviction for long-running jobs)
kubectl drain dpool-us-e1-07 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force
# pin new placement for lumenabio to dedicated-fallback-1
redwoodctl route update --tenant lumenabio --pool dedicated-fallback-1 --priority immediate
```

aaron (support): initiating failover route and increasing retry window on API gateways to reduce 502s. will also enable caching for critical endpoint /v1/embeddings for 15m.

jordan: draining now. eviction logs show some pods stuck at Terminating due to local scratch mounts. forcing delete for those two jobs (they'll restart from checkpoint).

ops-bot: NOTE: automatic fallback policy engaged for tenant lumenabio -> dedicated-fallback-1; sessions in-flight being drained. estimated completion 3-5m.

maya (oncall): Elena, please DM customers on status: affected: lumenabio-prod (10% traj requests degrade), lumenabio-staging (all requests fail until pods restart). message: "we've isolated a faulty GPU host and are failing your traffic to a warm standby pool; you may see transient retries up to 5 minutes."

elena (CS - LumenaBio): sending now. will attach soggy logs if they ask. also asking for ETA on node replacement.

jordan: node shows ECC + BMC fault after preempt. hardware flagged for RMA. opening hardware ticket with provider now (RMA-91287).

maya (oncall): are there any cross-tenant impacts? did fallback pool have capacity headroom?

jordan: dedicated-fallback-1 had ~30% spare. after shifting lumenabio, latency for other tenants unchanged. monitoring CPU/GPU queue to be safe.

eli (noc): logging: please add annotation to incident tracker: affected_customer:LumenaBio, pool:dpool-us-e1-07, mitigation:drain+fallback, hw_ticket:RMA-91287.

maya (oncall): will do. creating incident ticket: INC-20231106-247. linking runbook and timeline.

maya (oncall): handoff note for night oncall (@eli): node isolated and drained, tenant traffic on dedicated-fallback-1, hardware RMA opened, customer CS notified, watch for: any retry storms from queued jobs, backlog spike on embeddings, and failed job restarts. if fallback saturates, escalate to capacity-ops to spin temporary burst nodes.

eli (noc): taking handoff. I'll keep monitoring and will escalate to capacity-ops if GPU utilization > 75% for 5m.

aaron (support): post-mortem checklist: capture kernel oops, NVLink logs, BMC dump; confirm if preempt signal came from provider (we saw it); validate automatic caching prevented user-visible 5xxs for 90% of requests.

jordan: attaching quick logs snippet here:
```
[15:11:02] GPU1: ECC error threshold exceeded
[15:11:03] kernel: nvidia 0000:65:00.0: GPU fault: 0x35e1
[15:11:04] cloud-agent: preempt_signal received for instance i-0a1b2c3d
[15:11:05] kubelet: eviction - pod lumenabio-embed-xyz terminating
```

maya (oncall): thanks. next steps: 1) monitor fallback pool stability (eli), 2) ensure RMA progress and plan for replacement node (jordan), 3) update customer thread with "we'll follow up with root cause and remediation within 24 hours" (elena), 4) write short blameless incident note once stable (maya).

elena (CS - LumenaBio): customers acknowledged and appreciate the quick failover. asking about durable mitigation to avoid repeated preempts — can we offer persistent reserved capacity instead of spot-backed?

jordan: good call — for enterprise VPC/dedicated customers we should propose reserved-backed nodes or dedicated hardware to prevent cloud preemptions. will include options in follow-up.

eli (noc): Confirming handoff: I'm monitoring charts, channel set to DND-off alerts, will ping if any regressions.

maya (oncall): closing active paging for this thread. if any new alerts, reopen with thread_ts 1718504321. :white_check_mark:"
